title: SNAP participation, processing timeliness, and direct access are distinct state-level signals
source_unit: Official USDA/FNA state-level SNAP participation, application timeliness, recertification timeliness, and Program Access Index tables
geography: United States; 50 states and District of Columbia

denominator.unit: matched state/DC aggregates common to participation, APT, RPT, and PAI extraction

snap_participation.unit: percent of state population; FY2025 average monthly participant rate; state-rate distribution

application_timeliness.unit: percent timely among applications subject to the FY2025 APT measure

recertification_timeliness.unit: percent timely among recertifications subject to the FY2025 RPT measure

participation_vs_application_timeliness.unit: unweighted Pearson correlation across state/DC aggregates

participation_vs_recertification_timelin.unit: unweighted Pearson correlation across state/DC aggregates

observations.method: Joined official FY2025 USDA participation chart data to the official FY2025 FNA APT and RPT state tables by state name; summarized the 51 common state/DC aggregates and calculated unweighted Pearson screens.
observations.uncertainty: Ecological descriptive comparison; APT and RPT have distinct quality-control universes, routing rules, and case mix. No causal identification, population weighting, margin-of-error propagation, or household-level inference.
observations.subgroup: All 50 states and DC; territories excluded because the companion participation crosswalk is defined for states/DC.
observations.counterinterpretation: A low participation rate can coexist with strong route timeliness, and a high participation rate can coexist with weak route timeliness. Participation is not an administrative performance score.

observations.period: Calendar year 2023 compared with FY2025 participation; 50 states and DC

denominator.unit: matched state/DC aggregates in the 2023 PAI and FY2025 participation extraction

program_access_index_2023.unit: ratio of average monthly participants to people with income below 125 percent FPL

participation_vs_program_access_index.unit: unweighted Pearson correlation across state/DC aggregates

observations.method: Joined the official 2023 USDA/FNA PAI state table to FY2025 USDA participation rates by state name; summarized the common state/DC aggregates and calculated an unweighted Pearson screen.
observations.uncertainty: PAI is not a strict eligible-population take-up rate and can exceed 1 because its denominator is people below 125 percent FPL. The period differs from FY2025; the strong association is partly expected from the construction of the index.
observations.counterinterpretation: The PAI association is not independent confirmation of the participation rate and cannot establish why a state has high or low access.

denominator.unit: state/DC aggregates; named counterexamples selected from the common extraction

observations.method: Selected named state/DC rows from the reproducible extraction to test whether participation orders states in the same way as administrative route measures.
observations.uncertainty: Counterexamples are descriptive and do not identify causes; differences may reflect eligibility composition, geography, case mix, system design, staffing, applicant behavior, or measurement rules.
observations.subgroup: Selected state/DC counterexamples, not a representative subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: A named state's combination of rates does not explain household experience or prove agency performance without finer-grained administrative and household evidence.

boundary: This layer distinguishes population participation, application-route timeliness, recertification-route timeliness, and a low-income access index. It does not establish household-level access, eligible nonparticipation, food security, administrative causality, political response, or cultural meaning. The committed layer hash covers the detailed interpretation and summary; the reproduction script preserves the full state-by-state extraction path.
